Privacy.title: JaoPor privacy policy
Privacy.intro: JaoPor (jaopor.vercel.app) is a directory of things people build with AI, with numbers verified at the source. This page explains what we collect, why, how long we keep it, and what you control.

items.t: You sign in with Google or GitHub. We receive your name, email and profile picture from that provider and use them to create your account and show your name/picture on your projects and profile.
We never see or store your Google or GitHub password.
Account data is stored in a Supabase database (Singapore region).

sections.title: 2. Project and profile information you enter

items.t: Project details (name, description, links, screenshots, etc.) are public once you publish.
Builder profiles: you choose per field (e.g. province, social links, experience, skills) whether it's shown to everyone, signed-in members only, or hidden, and you can leave the builders directory.
The LINE ID and contact email you add are shown only to people whose contact request you accept.

Product updates, comments and images you post are public. Images are resized and converted in your browser, and location data (EXIF) is removed before upload. A post's author sees who liked it; everyone else sees only the count.

sections.title: 3. Numbers from connected services (revenue, GitHub activity and visitor counts)

items.t: API keys you connect (e.g. Stripe) must be read-only. We encrypt them before storing and decrypt them only on our server when fetching numbers.
We store aggregate numbers only (e.g. 30-day revenue, MRR, visitor counts), never your customers' data.

sections.title: 4. The JaoPor visitor counter (the snippet founders add to their own sites)

items.t: Each page view on a site using the snippet sends one beacon. No cookies.
Our server computes a keyed hash (HMAC) of the IP address and user agent with a key that changes daily, to count unique visitors per day. The IP address is not stored.
Hashes from previous days are deleted once they are rolled up into a daily total; only the daily visitor count remains.

sections.title: 5. "Who's here right now" (the live visitor map)
sections.body: This section shows, anonymously, how many people have JaoPor open.

items.t: your browser generates a random ID stored on your device (localStorage), a made-up name from a fixed word list we control (e.g. "Blue Elephant") and a cartoon avatar drawn from that ID. It is not linked to your account.

our host (Vercel) estimates location from your IP address. We use only the country, the nearest province (in Thailand), and coordinates rounded to about 11 km plus a small random offset. Your IP address is not stored and is never shared with other visitors.

items.b: What other visitors see while you're online:
items.t: your made-up name and avatar, the type of page you're on (e.g. "a project page"), device type (mobile/desktop), country or province, and the approximate point on the world map.
only while a JaoPor tab is visible on your screen; it disconnects when you switch tabs. This runs on Supabase Realtime and is not stored permanently; it disappears when you leave.

while a page is open, your browser sends a signal about once a minute so the count works even if the live connection fails. We store: a hash of your anonymous ID (daily-changing key), the page path, country/province, device type and last-seen time. Entries older than 10 minutes are deleted automatically.
press "Don't show me" under the map (or the button below); this browser then stops sending both (you can still watch). Press × to hide the section from the home page.
when you press "World", your browser loads map images directly from OpenFreeMap, which, like any website you load, sees your IP address.

sections.title: 6. What's stored in your browser
sections.body: No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies. Stored on your device: the sign-in cookie (signed-in users only), theme, currency, the province you picked in the Olympics, the live map's anonymous ID, and your hide/opt-out choices. You can clear them in your browser settings.

items.t: A chat opens only when a contact request is accepted. Only you and the other person can read it.
Messages are stored in JaoPor's database (Supabase) and are not end-to-end encrypted. The JaoPor team reads a message only when it is reported, to check for abuse.
You can block at any time: the chat closes, no new messages can be sent, and your LINE / email stop being shared.
Up to 200 messages a day.

sections.title: 8. Services we use
sections.body: Vercel (hosting), Supabase (database, sign-in, realtime), Google and GitHub (sign-in), OpenFreeMap (world map images, only when you open it), Google Gemini (when a project owner presses "Fill from website", public text from that project's website is sent for a summary), Frankfurter (exchange rates, server-side, no user data).

items.t: Delete a project yourself from the dashboard.

To delete your account, contact jaopordev@gmail.com. Deleting an account removes your profile, skills, experience, follows, contact requests and project memberships, plus your posts, images, comments (shown as 'comment deleted' where others replied) and the messages you sent. (A self-service delete button is being built.)

sections.title: 10. Changes
sections.body: When we change how we collect or use data, we update this page and the date above.

Security.title: How we handle your API keys
Security.intro: JaoPor shows revenue and GitHub activity verified from the services you already use, and visitor counts from our script or your analytics. This page explains which keys we accept, how we store them, and how you can revoke them.
Security.contact: Found a vulnerability or have a security question? Contact:

sections.title: 1. Read-only access only
sections.body: Before we store a key, we check every time that it can't write or change anything in your account. If it can, we reject it and don't keep it.

items.t: only restricted keys (starting with rk_live_ or rk_test_). Full-access secret keys (sk_) are rejected. We send empty update requests for records that don't exist; the key must be told “no permission” to pass.
the secret key (v2) must have no write permission. We check it the same way before storing it.
the API token must have only Account Analytics: Read. If it can reach zones, Workers or account settings, we reject it, and we only read your project's own domain.
Plausible Stats API keys are read-only by design; Umami uses a view-only share link.
no key needed. We read public repos only, and the repo must belong to the GitHub account you signed in with (or an organisation you're a public member of).
a snippet you add to your own site. No key involved.
Keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are saved. The decryption key is kept separately on the server only, not in the database.
Keys are decrypted only on the server when numbers are fetched. They are never sent back to the browser and never logged. After saving, you only see the last few characters to recognise the key.
The table that holds keys can't be read by any user or browser, including the project's owner.
We store totals only, such as MRR, 30-day and all-time revenue, active subscriptions, visitor counts, and daily figures for the charts.
We never store your customers' data, such as names, emails or card details.
Verified numbers are public on your project page, labelled with the service that verified them.

sections.title: 4. When numbers update
sections.body: Numbers are fetched once a day (around 3 AM Thailand time) and whenever you press “Refresh” in your dashboard.

items.t: Disconnect a revenue or traffic source in your dashboard: the encrypted key, and that source's numbers and daily history, are deleted immediately.
You can also revoke the key at the provider, for example in Stripe under Developers → API keys. The numbers then stop updating and your dashboard shows that the connection no longer works.
Deleting a project deletes all of its keys.
